name: Matter Milestone Updates

parameters.content:
## Matter Milestone Updates

### How it works

1. Runs once a day. Fetches the firm's user directory, then every Clio matter updated in roughly the last 2 days (a small overlap buffer so a daily cron running a bit late never misses one).
2. Drops any matter whose client has no email on file, then compares each remaining matter's current status against the last status this workflow saw for it — stored in n8n's own workflow static data, no external database or extra lookup call needed. The first time this workflow ever sees a given matter, it's cached silently without sending — there's no way to know what the status was before that first sighting.
3. If the status genuinely changed, looks it up in a firm-edited, plain-English message map. A status with no configured message (e.g. an internal-only status) is silently skipped — no client email.
4. Builds the update (styled HTML + plain text), personalized with the assigned attorney's name where resolvable, checks it against the compliance guardrail, then sends it if approved.

### Why a daily poll instead of a webhook

An earlier version of this template used a Clio webhook for instant delivery. Live testing surfaced a lot of friction that isn't worth it for most firms: there's no Settings UI for webhooks (API-only registration only), it requires its own OAuth scope, a newly created webhook silently sits in 'pending' and delivers nothing until a one-time verification handshake is answered correctly, subscriptions expire every 31 days, and a firm's day-to-day 'status' (e.g. a custom practice-area workflow stage) may not even be the same field as Clio's built-in Open/Pending/Closed status that webhooks watch. Polling once a day removes all of that — same dedupe, build, compliance, and send logic, just triggered by a schedule instead of a webhook — at the cost of up to a day of delay.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Set up the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) first — every client-facing update here goes through it.
- [ ] Configure Clio OAuth2 credentials with matter and user-directory read scope (reuse the credential from other templates in this catalog if already deployed).
- [ ] Configure SMTP credentials for sending.
- [ ] Edit the STATUS_MESSAGES map in 'Look Up Status Update Message' to match your firm's actual Clio matter statuses and firm-approved plain-English copy — this is the one node every firm must customize before going live.
- [ ] Set the required n8n Variables: CLIO_BASE_URL, FIRM_NAME, FIRM_EMAIL, FIRM_FROM_EMAIL, GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID.
- [ ] Activate the workflow. No webhook URL to wire anywhere.

### Customization

The STATUS_MESSAGES map is the entire content surface — add one entry per Clio status your firm wants to notify clients about. Everything else (fetch, dedupe, personalization, compliance) is generic and doesn't need editing.

## Fetch matters and detect changes

Pulls the firm's user directory, then every matter Clio has recorded as updated in roughly the last 2 days. Drops any matter whose client has no email on file — it can never be emailed regardless of what its status does.

## Detect real changes and look up the message

Compares each matter's current status against the last one this workflow saw for it — using n8n's own static data, no database — then looks a genuine change up in a firm-edited, plain-English message map. A status with no configured message is treated as internal-only and silently skipped (ABA Op. 512).

## Build, check, and send

Builds the personalized update, routes it through the compliance guardrail for opt-out checking and the required disclaimer, then sends it if approved.

nodes.name: Check Matter Statuses Daily
nodes.notes: Fires every day at 8am (n8n server timezone) — adjust the cron expression if a different time suits your firm better. Replaces an earlier webhook-based design: live testing found Clio webhooks required an API-only registration flow, a separate OAuth scope, a one-time verification handshake that silently failed if unanswered, 31-day expiring subscriptions, and uncertainty about whether a firm's day-to-day 'status' is even the same field Clio's matter webhooks watch. A daily poll sidesteps all of that using the exact same Clio credential and dedupe logic — at the cost of up to a day of delay instead of instant delivery.

nodes.name: Fetch Firm Users From Clio
nodes.notes:
Fetches the firm's user directory — used by 'Build Status Update Email' to resolve a matter's responsible_attorney id to a real name and email, so the update can be personalized. Requesting 'email' works here because /users.json is the primary resource, not a nested association (Clio rejects a nested User's email — confirmed live in PAC-63).

Runs first in this single linear chain, feeding straight into the matters fetch next — a genuine sequential dependency, not a disconnected side-fetch (confirmed live in PAC-63/64 that a disconnected side-fetch referenced only by name in code isn't reliably executed by n8n).

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as PAC-18/20/55/57/58/59/61/63/64/65 — reuse it if already deployed.

nodes.name: Fetch Recently Updated Matters From Clio
nodes.notes:
Fetches every matter Clio has recorded as updated in roughly the last 2 days — not just today's, so a cron that runs a bit late (server restart, holiday) never silently misses one. No status filter (e.g. status=Open) on purpose: a matter transitioning all the way to Closed still needs to be caught, and filtering to Open would make it disappear from this fetch the moment it closes, before the change is ever detected.

'updated_since' (ISO-8601 timestamp) and one level of nested 'client{...}' are both confirmed Clio API v4 conventions used elsewhere in this catalog. Firms with more than 200 matters updated in a 2-day window (unlikely for the 1-10 attorney firms this catalog targets) would need pagination added — check 'meta.paging.next' on this node's output if you suspect matters are being missed.

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as the user directory fetch above.

nodes.name: Split Out Matter Records
nodes.notes: Turns the single API response into one n8n item per matter, so the Filter and Code nodes downstream can each operate on individual matters. An empty or missing 'data' array (e.g. after a Clio error, or genuinely no matters updated recently) simply produces zero items — nothing downstream runs.

nodes.name: Filter Matters With Client Email
nodes.notes: Drops any matter whose client has no email on file (or has no client at all — internal/business matters, conflict-check placeholders, etc.). No point computing a status change for a matter this workflow could never email anyway.

nodes.name: Check If Status Actually Changed
nodes.notes: Static data is local to this n8n instance's execution store — it won't sync across multiple workers if the instance ever moves to queue mode. Fine for the single-instance deployment this template targets; flag it if the firm later scales to a multi-worker n8n setup.

nodes.name: If Status Actually Changed
nodes.notes:
Yes (status genuinely differs from what this workflow last saw for this matter) → look up whether there's a client message for it.
No (first time seeing this matter, or its status hasn't moved since the last run) → route to Skip.

nodes.name: Skip — Status Unchanged Or First Seen
nodes.notes: Either this matter's status hasn't actually changed since the last run, or this is the first time this workflow has ever seen it. No email sent either way.

nodes.name: Look Up Status Update Message
nodes.notes: The one node every firm must customize before going live — the STATUS_MESSAGES map is the entire content surface of this template. Status names must match Clio's exact status text (case-sensitive) or the lookup silently misses.

nodes.name: If Status Has Configured Message
nodes.notes:
Yes (this status has a firm-approved message configured) → build and send the update.
No (an internal-only or unconfigured status) → route to Skip. No email sent.

nodes.name: Skip — No Client Message For This Status
nodes.notes: This status genuinely changed, but the firm hasn't configured a client-facing message for it — treated as internal-only. No email sent.

nodes.name: Build Status Update Email
nodes.notes: Do not add an opt-out footer to 'message' (the plain-text body) — the compliance guardrail (next node) appends it automatically to that version and logs the send attempt. 'email_html' carries its own independently-built matching footer, since the guardrail never sees or touches the HTML version.

nodes.name: Check Compliance Before Sending
nodes.notes:
Checks whether this client has opted out of firm emails. If not, appends the required unsubscribe footer and logs the send attempt to the audit sheet — same client-facing pattern as PAC-18/64/65.

The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable.

Returns: { approved, message_out, recipient, suppression_reason } plus all upstream fields — note this REPLACES $json, so any field the build step added (like email_html) is not carried forward automatically; downstream nodes that need it must reach back to $('Build Status Update Email').item.json explicitly (confirmed the hard way in PAC-65 — reading $json.email_html here sent a blank email).

nodes.name: If Update Approved
nodes.notes:
Yes (client hasn't opted out) → send.
No (client has opted out of firm emails) → route to Skip. The suppression is already logged by the guardrail.

nodes.name: Send Status Update Email
nodes.notes:
Sends the compliance-approved update to the client — both the plain-text body (message_out from the guardrail, carrying the required unsubscribe footer) and the styled HTML body. HTML and subject both reach back to 'Build Status Update Email' by name rather than reading $json, since the guardrail call immediately upstream replaced $json with its own response.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

nodes.name: Skip — Client Opted Out
nodes.notes: This client has opted out of firm emails. The suppression is already logged by the guardrail workflow. No email is sent.

main.node: Fetch Recently Updated Matters From Clio
Skip — Status Unchanged Or First Seen
Skip — No Client Message For This Status

description: Runs once a day: fetches every Clio matter updated in roughly the last 2 days (plus the firm's user directory), and compares each one's current status against the last status this workflow saw for it, using n8n's own workflow static data (no external database), so a client update only sends on a genuine status change, never a duplicate. Looks the new status up in a firm-edited, plain-English message map — an unconfigured status is treated as internal-only and skipped. Sends the matching update, personalized with the assigned attorney's name where resolvable, through the Bar-Compliance Guardrail. Replaces a paid Case Status app — poor communication between milestones is a top bar-complaint driver of client dissatisfaction.
